content_summary: SEBI's Board approved establishing a regulatory framework for ESG Rating Providers by inserting a new chapter into the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999, rather than a standalone accreditation-only scheme. The adopted framework created two tiers -- Category I and Category II ERPs -- with different net-worth and service-scope criteria, open to a wider pool of applicants than the CRA/RA-only eligibility proposed in the Jan 2022 anchor paper. It introduced a requirement that ERPs consider India/Emerging-Market parameters, a 'Core ESG Rating' tied to assured BRSR Core data, and (per the intervening Feb 2023 consultation paper that fed the Board decision) allowed either an issuer-pays or a subscriber-pays model rather than mandating subscriber-pay as originally proposed.

key_parameters.name: entities eligible for ERP status
key_parameters.proposed: Only SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies and Research Analysts (Jan 2022 paper)
key_parameters.final: Any entity meeting Category I or Category II registration criteria under a new CRA Regulations chapter -- not limited to existing CRAs/RAs

key_parameters.name: minimum net worth
key_parameters.proposed: Flat Rs. 10 crore (in addition to existing CRA/RA net worth)
key_parameters.final: Category I: liquid net worth >= Rs. 5 crore ongoing / Rs. 10 crore at application; Category II: >= Rs. 10 lakh ongoing / Rs. 20 lakh at application

key_parameters.name: ERP business/payment model
key_parameters.final: Either issuer-pays or subscriber-pays permitted (hybrid disallowed)

notes: The Jan 2022 anchor was an early concept paper; a fuller follow-on consultation (Feb 22, 2023, evidence E02) with the Category I/II structure preceded the Board's Mar 29, 2023 approval, whose PR is used as decisive_date (earliest official adoption per protocol). The SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023 gazette notification followed later; not separately re-verified since it postdates the board PR and cannot be an earlier decisive date. content_label_confidence=medium: structure (Cat I/II, net worth) verified from board-meeting agenda note; business-model parameter inferred from the intervening Feb-2023 CP, not independently re-checked against the final Master Circular text.

content_summary: At its Dec 20, 2022 meeting, the SEBI Board approved amendments to the Buy-back Regulations, 2018 that reduced the buyback-tender-offer timeline by 18 days -- going beyond the consultation paper's proposed mechanism by removing the draft-letter-of-offer filing/SEBI-observation step entirely (rather than merely shortening it from T+10 to T+5) and compressing the tendering/payment period. This was formally notified via the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023 (gazetted Feb 7, 2023, effective Mar 9, 2023). The Dec 20, 2022 board press release, searched in full, contains no mention of a matching amendment to Open Offer timelines under the Takeover Regulations, 2011 -- i.e., as far as verified, the paper's other proposal (62 to 42 working days for open offers) was not acted on by the same decisive document.

key_parameters.name: buyback tender-offer completion timeline
key_parameters.proposed: 43 working days reduced to 36 working days, largely via shortening (not removing) the draft-letter-of-offer step
key_parameters.final: Reduced by 18 working days by eliminating the draft-letter-of-offer/SEBI-observation requirement altogether, plus a shorter tendering/payment period

key_parameters.name: open offer completion timeline (Takeover Regulations)
key_parameters.proposed: 62 working days reduced to 42 working days
key_parameters.final: Not confirmed adopted in the Dec 20, 2022 board decision or any other document found before censor date

notes: decisive_date uses the earliest official adopting document (board PR, Dec 20 2022) per protocol, ahead of the Feb 7 2023 gazette notification of the same amendments. content_label_confidence lowered because the open-offer/Takeover-Regulations half of the anchor's proposal could not be confirmed adopted (a targeted search found no matching SAST timeline amendment); it may simply not have been located, or may remain unresolved -- flagged rather than guessed.
